_note: The coach's intention (2026-11-13, plan L0-CLOSE step 9, OI-27): it modulates the default, it does not replace it. A high block pushes the line high_block_line_cm up and closer to the ball out of possession (the line behind the ball shrinks by half as much); a low block drops it low_block_line_cm and sits further behind the ball; a wide team stretches its width with the ball by width_change_milli, a narrow one shrinks it. The default (mid, normal) is the block below, unchanged. The team block: what a side does without instructions (VISION §3, the role as a default intention, 2026-11-12). Each outfield player keeps his role's place inside a block: depth from the defensive line (0) to the forward line (1), and width from left (0) to right (1), read from the formation. The block follows the ball: the defensive line sits behind the ball (further behind and higher up the pitch when the side has the ball), within a minimum and a maximum distance from its own goal; the block shifts towards the ball's side. With the ball the side stretches (longer, wider), without it it compacts (shorter, narrower). The coach's instructions (L2) will move these numbers; they never script the players.
_source: Order of magnitude of a real team's shape: a compact block out of possession is about 30-35 m deep. width_in_possession_cm, width_out_of_possession_cm and ball_side_shift_milli (2026-11-15, SIM 127, OI-100) are measured on the Metrica Sports sample tracking data, Sample Games 1 and 2 (github.com/metrica-sports/sample-data, anonymised, 25 frames a second, sampled once a second, the goalkeepers left out, possession from the synchronised events): the distance between a side's two widest outfield players, with the ball in play (the tracking's ball present: the block of open play, not the gathering at a restart), is 47.2, 48.4, 46.0 and 47.6 m with the ball (mean 47.3), 37.0, 38.0, 36.7 and 36.2 m without it (mean 37.0); counting the dead-ball frames too it was 42.2 and 37.4 (SIM 127, corrected at SIM 129); the slope of the side's centre (halfway between its widest players) on the ball's distance from the middle is 0.24, 0.21, 0.26, 0.22 with the ball and 0.29, 0.29, 0.31, 0.31 without it (mean 0.27). The block's width is therefore the distance between its widest players. Two matches: a small sample, to be widened at L3. The other values are arbitrary, declared, to be calibrated at L3.
